statements.dynamics: Dynamics is the study of the forces that cause objects and systems to move. Kinematics describes how an object moves, and dynamics asks why it moves that way; Newton’s laws of motion are its foundation.
statements.force: A force is a push or a pull, and it has both a magnitude and a direction, so it is a vector and adds as other vectors add.
statements.free-body-diagram: A free-body diagram draws the body as a single point and every external force acting on it as an arrow from that point, so the forces can be added without the picture of the situation getting in the way.
statements.newtons-second-law: The acceleration of a system is directly proportional to the net external force on it and in the same direction, and inversely proportional to its mass. It is a relation among three quantities that can each be measured on their own, not a definition.
statements.newton-unit: The SI unit of force is defined from Newton’s second law: one newton is the force that accelerates a one-kilogram system at one meter per second squared.
statements.mass-versus-weight: Mass is the quantity of matter and does not change with place; weight is the gravitational force on that mass and does. The two words are used interchangeably in everyday language, but in physics they mean different things.
statements.friction: Friction is a force that opposes the motion past each other of objects that are touching. It is an external force, and it is what slows a sliding object down.
statements.thrust: Thrust is the forward reaction force on a rocket that throws gas backward: it pushes hard on the gas, and by the third law the gas pushes just as hard forward on the rocket. Thrust drives rockets, airplanes and cars.
statements.inertial-frame: An inertial frame of reference is a frame that is neither accelerating nor rotating, and only in such a frame do Newton’s laws take their simple forms. In an accelerating frame an observer sees forces with no physical origin, such as the westward push on a satellite seen from a rotating Earth, and those fictitious forces are an artifact of the frame.
statements.drag-force: A drag force is the frictional force a fluid such as air or water exerts on an object moving through it, and like any friction it opposes the motion.

new.name: System
new.statement: A system is the object or collection of objects being observed, defined by its boundaries. All forces originating from outside the system are external forces.

new.name: Free-body diagram
new.statement: A free-body diagram is a sketch showing all of the external forces acting on an object or system, with the system represented by a dot and the forces by arrows extending outward from it.
